al-sos-2026-sl-general-sample-ballots.note: 67 county sample ballots (PDF; every ballot style of the county drawn one over another), read in drawing order style by style; only the offices, names, parties, order and Write-in lines of the state contests are kept (al_2026_general_sample_ballots_state.json). The sha256 here is of the list of the files' own SHA-256s. Every 2026 style of every county prints each race the same way unless named in the loader's report. The State Certifications of candidates (August 26, 2026) are scans with no text, so the typeset sample ballots are read instead. A ballot shows no withdrawn candidates and no declared write-ins, so none are loaded. Ballot order as printed. Names printed in capitals are shown in ordinary capitals.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 all 67 Alabama counties elect a sheriff, 60 a coroner and 65 a revenue commissioner or a tax assessor and a tax collector; 48 elect members of the county commission, 58 members of the county board of education and 10 the county superintendent of education. No county's November ballot has a contest for judge of probate, circuit clerk, district attorney or constable. Cities and towns vote at their own municipal elections, not in November: the Secretary of State's calendars give August 26, 2025 for the regular municipal elections, which Act 2021-157 moved from 2024, and August 25, 2026 for those held this year.
local_calendar.s: Alabama Secretary of State, Elections Division: the 67 county sample ballots for November 3, 2026; 2026 Municipal Election FCPA Filing Calendar; 2025 Municipal Election FCPA Filing Calendar; 2026 Candidate Filing Guide

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the 67 county sample ballots the Secretary of State posted for November 3, 2026: every county office and county board of education contest printed on them, 458 contests and 529 candidates in all 67 counties (county commission seats 137, county board of education seats 100, sheriff 67, coroner 60, revenue commissioner 58, county superintendents of education 10, tax assessor 7, tax collector 7, county commission chairmen 6, license commissioner 3, assistant tax assessor 1, assistant tax collector 1, racing commissioner 1). Every one is a partisan office, and names, parties and ballot order are as printed. A sample ballot shows no one who withdrew and names no write-in candidates; candidates for county office are certified to each county's judge of probate rather than to the Secretary of State, so these ballots are the statewide official source for them. Not loaded: constitutional amendments and other ballot questions, the May 19 primary and June 16 runoff for county offices, and city and town offices, which are not on this ballot. One contest is printed with a Write-in line and no name.
local_coverage.s: Alabama Secretary of State, Elections Division: 2026 General Election Sample Ballots, one for each county; 2026 Administrative Calendar
